raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

`lamport_workspace.py` exchanges the CUDA IPC handles of the MiniMax fused allreduce+RMSNorm workspace through `cudaIpcMemHandle_t.reserved`. cuda-bindings 13 (the version pinned for CUDA 13 builds, e.g. `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt`) no longer exposes that attribute, so on every CUDA 13 build the workspace fails to initialize:

```text
Failed to initialize MiniMax fused allreduce+RMSNorm Lamport workspace: 'cuda.bindings.runtime.cudaIpcMemHandle_t' object has no attribute 'reserved'. This is expected on GPUs without P2P (IPC peer access) support. Falling back to the eager allreduce + RMSNorm path.
```

The warning blames missing P2P support, and MiniMax-M2 TP runs on such builds silently use the slower eager path (the TP=4 server log below prints it 124 times, once per layer and rank). `tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py` fails on such builds for the same reason.

This PR reads and writes the 64 handle bytes through `getPtr()` (`ctypes.string_at` / `ctypes.memmove`), which cuda-bindings 12 and 13 both provide, instead of the `reserved` attribute.

## Test Plan

- `tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py` on a GB300 node (CUDA 13 build, cuda-bindings 13.4.3) on two of its GPUs, before and after the change.
- `vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5 -tp 4` on the same node before and after the change: count of the warning in the server log.

## Test Result

```text
# cuda-bindings on the node
CUDA-BINDINGS: 13.4.3

# before (main at d09ff7763)
COMMAND: python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py
FAILED tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py::test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk[42-1e-06-dtype0-hidden_dims0-1-2]
FAILED tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py::test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk[42-1e-06-dtype0-hidden_dims0-128-2]
FAILED tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py::test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk[42-1e-06-dtype0-hidden_dims0-333-2]
FAILED tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py::test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk[42-1e-06-dtype1-hidden_dims0-1-2]
FAILED tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py::test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk[42-1e-06-dtype1-hidden_dims0-128-2]
FAILED tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py::test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk[42-1e-06-dtype1-hidden_dims0-333-2]
AttributeError: 'cuda.bindings.runtime.cudaIpcMemHandle_t' object has no attribute 'reserved'
6 failed, 90 passed, 13 skipped, 14 warnings in 123.11s (0:02:03)

# after (this PR)
COMMAND: python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py
96 passed, 13 skipped, 14 warnings in 129.54s (0:02:09)
```

With the fix, `vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5 -tp 4` on that node no longer prints the warning (see the server-log excerpt below).

```text
# main (eager fallback), same node, same command apart from the port:
COMMAND: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8501 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remo
$ grep -c 'Lamport workspace' main_tp4_server.log
124
WARNING 10-10 02:29:32 [rms_norm_tp.py:327] Failed to initialize MiniMax fused allreduce+RMSNorm Lamport workspace: 'cuda.bindings.runtime.cudaIpcMemHandle_t' object has no attribute 'reserved'. This is expected on GPUs without P2P (IPC peer access) support. Falling back to the eager allreduce + RMS

# this PR (fused kernel active):
COMMAND: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8512 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remo
$ grep -c 'Lamport workspace' pr_tp4_server.log
0
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

Note for anyone who already served a MiniMax-M2 model on a CUDA 13 build: the fused kernel changes the compiled graph, and a `torch.compile` cache written before this change is reused as is (its key does not cover this file). On the node above that showed up as `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 10)` inside the cached graph during the profile run; starting once with `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` (or clearing `~/.cache/vllm/torch_compile_cache`) fixes it. I did not change the cache key here.

files.patch:
@@ -4,6 +4,7 @@
 
 import array
 import contextlib
+import ctypes
 import struct
 import sys
 import threading
@@ -59,6 +60,22 @@ def _cuda_memcpy_d2d(dst: int, src: int, size: int):
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
 
+# sizeof(cudaIpcMemHandle_t): CUDA_IPC_HANDLE_SIZE
+_IPC_HANDLE_SIZE = 64
+
+
+def _ipc_handle_to_bytes(handle) -> bytes:
+    # cuda-bindings 12.x exposes the raw struct as ``reserved``; 13.x only
+    # exposes the pointer, so read the bytes through it on both.
+    return ctypes.string_at(handle.getPtr(), _IPC_HANDLE_SIZE)
+
+
+def _ipc_handle_from_bytes(data: bytes):
+    handle = cudart.cudaIpcMemHandle_t()
+    ctypes.memmove(handle.getPtr(), data, _IPC_HANDLE_SIZE)
+    return handle
+
+
 class IpcBuffer:
     """Allocates CUDA device memory and exchanges IPC handles with all ranks
     so that every rank holds a valid device pointer to every other rank's buffer.
@@ -84,15 +101,16 @@ def __init__(self, rank: int, world_size: int, size: int, process_group=None):
 
         all_handles: list[bytes | None] = [None] * world_size
         torch.distributed.all_gather_object(
-            all_handles, bytes(local_handle.reserved), group=process_group
+            all_handles, _ipc_handle_to_bytes(local_handle), group=process_group
         )
 
         for r in range(world_size):
             if r == rank:
                 self.peer_ptrs[r] = self.local_ptr
             else:
-                handle = cudart.cudaIpcMemHandle_t()
-                handle.reserved = all_handles[r]
+                peer_handle = all_handles[r]
+                assert peer_handle is not None
+                handle = _ipc_handle_from_bytes(peer_handle)
                 err, ptr = cudart.cudaIpcOpenMemHandle(
                     handle, cudart.cudaIpcMemLazyEnablePeerAccess
                 )
